claim: Plants release herbivory-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) from an herbivore's first bite.
source_text: From an herbivore's first bite, plants release herbivory-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs)
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established fact in plant biology presented as background knowledge.

claim: HIPVs can attract enemies of herbivores.
source_text: From an herbivore's first bite, plants release herbivory-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) which can attract enemies of herbivores.
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge supported by prior literature, as indicated by the context of the introduction.

claim: Other animals and competing plants can intercept HIPVs for their own use.
source_text: However, other animals and competing plants can intercept HIPVs for their own use
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge about the complexity of HIPV signaling in ecological communities.

evidence_reasoning: This statement identifies a gap in scientific knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: HIPV-emitting N. attenuata plants produced twice as many buds and flowers as HIPV-silenced plants in a 2-year field study.
source_text: In a 2-year field study, HIPV-emitting N. attenuata plants produced twice as many buds and flowers as HIPV-silenced plants
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the experimental data collected in the field study.

claim: The fitness benefit of HIPV emission occurred only when native Geocoris spp. predators reduced herbivore loads by 50% on HIPV-emitters.

evidence_reasoning: This describes the conditional nature of the fitness benefit observed in the experimental data.

claim: TPI-producing plants were not fitter than TPI-silenced plants.
source_text: TPI-producing plants were not fitter than TPI-silenced plants
evidence_reasoning: This is a negative result from the experimental comparison of plant fitness.

source_text: TPIs weakened a specialist herbivore's behavioral evasive responses to simulated Geocoris spp. attack
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from behavioral assays conducted in the study.

claim: TPIs function against specialists by enhancing indirect defense.
source_text: TPIs function against specialists by enhancing indirect defense

claim: Plant indirect defenses are traits that disable or remove herbivores by manipulating tri-trophic interactions to the advantage of the plant.
source_text: Plant indirect defenses are traits that disable or remove herbivores by manipulating tri-trophic interactions to the advantage of the plant

claim: Indirect defenses include domatia, extrafloral nectar, and food bodies which provide shelter and nutrition for predators and parasitoids.
source_text: Indirect defenses are widespread and include domatia, extrafloral nectar, and food bodies which provide shelter and nutrition for predators and parasitoids

claim: irLOX2 plants suffered 60% less mirid and noctuid damage by the end of M3 in 2011.
source_text: although irLOX2 plants suffered 60% less mirid and noctuid damage by the end of M3 in 2011
evidence_reasoning: This is a measurement showing reduced natural herbivore damage on GLV-deficient plants.

claim: Reduced herbivore damage on irLOX2 in 2011 cannot explain why irLOX2 plants displayed reduced growth and reproduction.
source_text: Reduced herbivore damage on irLOX2 in 2011 could have increased the growth and reproduction of irLOX2 plants relative to WT, but cannot explain why irLOX2 plants instead displayed reduced growth and reproduction.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical argument ruling out natural herbivore damage as an explanation for fitness differences.

claim: In 2010, matched plants received three lab strain M. sexta larvae per plant to a lower stem leaf.
source_text: Plants in 2010 received three lab strain M. sexta larvae per plant to a lower stem leaf.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental design for the 2010 matched plant assay.

claim: In the absence of Geocoris spp. in 2010, genotypes did not differ in M. sexta mortality or plant reproduction.
source_text: In the absence of Geocoris spp. in 2010, genotypes did not differ in M. sexta mortality (N=51 larvae)—which in every observed case was due to a failure of the larva to feed—or plant reproduction (N=17 plants)
evidence_reasoning: This is a key finding showing that fitness differences depend on predator presence.

claim: Flower removal itself does not cause a difference among genotypes.
source_text: This, and the fact that flower production did not differ among genotypes in 2011 through infestation M3 despite flower removal (Figure 6), indicates that flower removal itself does not cause a difference among genotypes
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the consistency of results across different flower removal protocols.

claim: In 2011, hemi-irLOX2, irPI and WT plants were matched prior to infestation M4 to exclude differences in growth, reproduction and Manduca spp. damage.
source_text: In 2011, hemi-irLOX2, irPI and WT plants were matched prior to infestation M4 to exclude differences in growth, reproduction and Manduca spp. damage arising during M. sexta infestations M2 and M3
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental design for the 2011 matched plant assay.

claim: All reproductive meristems were removed from matched plants in 2011 by cutting inflorescences at their base.
source_text: Instead of regularly removing flowers, we removed all reproductive meristems from matched plants in 2011 by cutting inflorescences at their base.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a methodological modification in the 2011 experiment.

claim: Native Manduca spp. moths oviposited on plants during the experiment.
source_text: Because oviposition by native Manduca spp. moths on plants during the experiment was unpredictable
evidence_reasoning: This describes a natural occurrence during the field experiment.

claim: Wild Manduca spp. neonates were collected from natural ovipositions and used for infestation M4.
source_text: we collected wild Manduca spp. neonates from natural ovipositions and used them for infestation M4
evidence_reasoning: This describes the source of larvae for the final matched plant assay.

claim: Larval mortality reached a maximum of 76% after larvae transitioned from the second to third instar in 2011.
source_text: Larval mortality (upper panel) reached a maximum of 76% after larvae transitioned from the second to third instar (days 9 and 10)
evidence_reasoning: This is a measurement from the 2011 matched plant assay.

claim: Larval mortality on hemi-irLOX2 was only half as great as on WT or irPI at the time of maximum mortality.
source_text: at which time larval mortality on hemi-irLOX2 was only half as great as on WT or irPI
evidence_reasoning: This is a key finding showing differential predation rates in the matched plant assay.

claim: Larvae beyond the third instar are not susceptible to Geocoris spp.
source_text: larvae beyond this stage are not susceptible to Geocoris spp.
evidence_reasoning: This is a fact from cited literature (Kessler and Baldwin, 2001).

claim: By the end of the M4 assay, hemi-irLOX2 plants had produced 40–50% fewer buds and flowers than matched WT and irPI plants.
source_text: By the end of the assay, the hemi-irLOX2 plants had produced 40–50% fewer buds and flowers than matched WT and irPI plants
evidence_reasoning: This is the primary fitness measurement from the 2011 matched plant assay.

claim: Unripe seed capsules on hemi-irLOX2 plants were reduced by 50% compared to WT and irPI.
source_text: This reduced bud and flower production was not due to accelerated seed set: unripe seed capsules on hemi-irLOX2 plants were also reduced by 50%
evidence_reasoning: This measurement confirms that the fitness difference is real and not due to timing differences.

claim: Herbivore-induced GLV emissions function as indirect defenses by increasing predation of Manduca spp. larvae twofold, resulting in a twofold increase in bud and flower production for N. attenuata in its native habitat.
source_text: These data demonstrate that herbivore-induced GLV emissions function as indirect defenses by increasing predation of Manduca spp. larvae twofold, resulting in a twofold increase in bud and flower production for N. attenuata in its native habitat.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata did not differ in their growth or instar progression on plants.
source_text: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata did not differ in their growth or instar progression
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the analysis of larval performance by species.

claim: TPIs had a less consistent and negative effect on plant reproduction than expected.
source_text: TPIs had a less consistent and, contrary to our expectations, negative effect on
evidence_reasoning: This summarizes the unexpected findings regarding TPI effects on fitness (text appears cut off but meaning is clear from context).

claim: Wild Manduca spp. larvae fed on WT plants were 50% less likely to successfully attack an insect pin mimicking Geocoris spp. attack compared to larvae fed on irPI plants.
source_text: Similarly to the on-plant assay, larvae fed on WT leaves were 50% less likely to successfully attack the insect pin, either when initially poked, or poked and lifted with the pin
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the behavioral assays mimicking predator attack.

claim: WT-fed larvae ceased to grow for at least 24 hr after simulated attack, while irPI-fed larvae continued to grow.
source_text: We also monitored recovery post-trial and found that WT-fed larvae ceased to grow for at least 24 hr after simulated attack, while irPI-fed larvae continued to grow
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the behavioral assays showing differential recovery from simulated predation.

claim: TPIs may support indirect defense by weakening the response of larvae to predator attack.
source_text: Thus TPIs did not increase plant reproduction under attack from Manduca spp. in nature, but may support indirect defense by weakening the response of larvae to predator attack.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the behavioral data suggesting a mechanism for TPI function.

claim: The contradictory higher predation rates of Manduca spp. larvae from irPI than from WT plants might reflect Geocoris spp.'s feeding preference if irPI-fed larvae are more nutritious.
source_text: The contradictory higher predation rates of Manduca spp. larvae from irPI than from WT plants (Figure 5) might reflect Geocoris spp.'s feeding preference, if irPI-fed larvae are more nutritious than WT-fed larvae
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for an unexpected result, referencing a hypothesis from the literature (Kaplan and Thaler, 2011).

claim: The hemi-irLOX2 plants used were created by crossing homozygous irPI and irLOX2 plants.
source_text: The hemi-irLOX2 plants used in this study were created by crossing homozygous irPI and irLOX2 plants
evidence_reasoning: This describes the genetic construction of one of the plant lines used.

claim: The irPI construct was not active in the hemizygous state in hemi-irLOX2 plants.
source_text: but the irPI construct was not active in the hemizygous state
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation about the genetic behavior of the RNAi construct.

claim: Functional RNAi constructs may be rendered ineffective as a result of insufficient gene dosage.
source_text: It is common molecular biology knowledge that functional RNAi constructs may be rendered ineffective as a result of insufficient gene dosage
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in molecular biology (Travella et al., 2006).

claim: Gene dosage effects may occur when an RNAi construct is present in the hemizygous state.
source_text: which may occur when an RNAi construct is present in the hemizygous state
evidence_reasoning: This is a known phenomenon in molecular biology (García-Pérez et al., 2004).

claim: The 35S promoter which drives the transcription of the RNAi construct may be methylated, reducing the dose of RNAi in individual plants.
source_text: The 35S promoter which drives the transcription of the RNAi construct may also be methylated: an epigenetic effect which can reduce the dose of RNAi in individual plants within a single transformed line
evidence_reasoning: This describes a known epigenetic mechanism that can affect transgene expression.

claim: Fewer than 5% of buds and flowers are aborted by healthy field-grown N. attenuata plants.
source_text: For field-grown N. attenuata plants, fewer than 5% of buds and flowers (in total) are aborted by healthy (not diseased) plants
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from field experience with the study species.

claim: Abortion of buds and flowers in healthy N. attenuata plants seems always to be due to damage by insects.
source_text: and abortion seems always to be due to damage by insects
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from field experience with the study species.

claim: N. attenuata plants are self-compatible.
source_text: Plants are self-compatible
evidence_reasoning: This is a known characteristic of N. attenuata reproductive biology.

claim: More than 70% of seed set from plants in native N. attenuata populations results from fertilization via self-pollen.
source_text: and more than 70% of seed set from plants in native populations results from fertilization via self-pollen
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from cited literature (Sime and Baldwin, 2003).

claim: Numbers of buds and flowers correlate to lifetime seed capsule production in N. attenuata.
source_text: Thus numbers of buds and flowers correlate to lifetime seed capsule production
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference based on the low abortion rate and self-compatibility.

claim: Lifetime seed capsule production correlates to lifetime seed production in N. attenuata.
source_text: which in turn correlates to lifetime seed production
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the relationship between capsules and seeds.

claim: The transgenic lines used do not vary in seed mass or their seedling viability under laboratory conditions.
source_text: The transgenic lines used do not vary in seed mass or their seedling viability under laboratory conditions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a characterization of the transgenic lines showing they don't differ in seed quality.

claim: Reproductive meristems were removed from matched plants in 2011 to allow following plant reproduction over full Manduca spp. larval development without incurring ripe transgenic seed capsules.
source_text: We removed all reproductive meristems from matched plants in 2011 to allow us to follow plant reproduction over full Manduca spp. larval development without incurring ripe transgenic seed capsules.
evidence_reasoning: This explains the rationale for a methodological choice in the experimental design.

claim: These data set the stage for the use of HIPVs as part of integrated pest management strategies (IPM).
source_text: By indicating the long-sought indirect defensive function of HIPVs, these data set the stage for the use of HIPVs as part of integrated pest management strategies (IPM)
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the applied implications of the findings.

claim: IPM strategies rely in part on recruiting biological control agents to reduce pesticide use.
source_text: which rely in part on recruiting biological control agents to reduce pesticide use
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about IPM strategies (Horne and Page, 2008).

claim: Biological control agents used in IPM are usually naturally occurring generalist parasitoids and predators, such as Geocoris spp.
source_text: These agents are usually naturally occurring generalist parasitoids and predators, such as Geocoris spp.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about IPM strategies with examples from the literature (Eubanks and Denno, 1999, 2000; Allison and Hare, 2009; Allmann and Baldwin, 2010).

claim: HIPVs are produced by genotypes of most, if not all crop plants.
source_text: HIPVs are produced by genotypes of most, if not all crop plants
evidence_reasoning: This is general knowledge about the widespread occurrence of HIPVs in plants.

claim: IPM would benefit from selective breeding or engineering of HIPV emission rather than relying on controlled release dispensers.
source_text: and IPM would benefit from selective breeding or engineering of HIPV emission (Kos et al., 2009) rather than relying on alternatives such as controlled release dispensers
evidence_reasoning: This is a recommendation based on the findings and cited literature.

claim: Controlled release dispensers for HIPVs have mixed success and require large amounts of synthetic HIPVs.
source_text: which have mixed success and require large amounts of synthetic HIPVs
evidence_reasoning: This is a limitation of current technology from cited literature (Kaplan, 2012).

claim: PIs may be employed to enhance the efficiency of indirect defense, especially combined with toxins like Bt.
source_text: PIs may be employed to enhance the efficiency of indirect defense, especially combined with toxins like Bt that directly target herbivores and are safe for biological control agents.
evidence_reasoning: This is a recommendation for applied use based on the findings about TPI effects.

claim: There are growing concerns about field-evolved Bt resistance.
source_text: With growing concerns about field-evolved Bt resistance
evidence_reasoning: This is a current issue in agricultural biotechnology from cited literature (Liu et al., 2010).

claim: Indirect defenses promise an effective 'first line of defense' against agricultural pests.
source_text: indirect defenses promise an effective 'first line of defense' against agricultural pests
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion about the potential application of the findings.

claim: Not even specialist herbivores are likely to rapidly evolve resistance to indirect defenses.
source_text: to which not even specialist herbivores are likely to rapidly evolve resistance
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the evolutionary stability of indirect defenses.
